S1.why: Two words under the bracket; 'gratis' is the everyday Norwegian word for free of charge, 'fri' would mean unrestricted.

S2.why: An invitation in the imperative, the way Norwegian apps address 'du'; no limit word, no sales word, 16 characters.

S3.s: Alle %lld gratisplassene er brukt. Cutlingene dine er fortsatt gratis og virker som før.
S3.back: All 5 free-places-the are used. Cutlings-the your are still free and work as before.
S3.why: 'Gratisplass' names the five tiles as slots, used the same way in S5, S21 and M3; 'cutlingene dine' is the vocabulary file's own inflected form; 86 characters.

S4.why: Plain fact in 'du' form; item word inflected as a Norwegian plural in running text, lower case as in the vocabulary sentence.

S5.why: 'X av Y' is the natural Norwegian count; both numbers keep their English order, so no positional forms are needed.

S6.why: Mirrors 'gratisplasser': five free slots become 5 000 slots, matching the grid the sheet shows after buying; 'Plass til 5 000 cutlinger' ran one character over.

S7.s: Du kan lagre opptil %@ tekster og %lld bilder.
S7.back: You can save up-to 5 000 texts and 500 images.
S7.why: 'Tekst' and 'Bilder' from the vocabulary file; 'opptil' is the normal word for an upper limit; 48 characters.

S8.why: Norwegian lists three with commas and 'og', no comma before 'og'.

S9.s: Ett kjøp gjelder for alle enheter som er logget på Apple-kontoen din.
S9.back: One purchase applies for all devices that are logged on Apple-account-the your.
S9.why: Reuses the vocabulary file's phrase 'enheter som er logget på Apple-kontoen din' word for word; 69 characters.

S10.why: Accented 'én' is the standard Norwegian way to stress 'one' as a number, not the article.

S11.s: Ingen abonnement, ingen reklame og ingen registrering.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertising and no registration.
S11.why: 'Reklame' is what Norwegians call ads in apps; 'registrering' says no sign-up without confusing it with the Apple Account mentioned above.

S12.why: The wording Norwegian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: Present tense of the same verb, closed with the single ellipsis character and no space, as iOS writes progress labels.

S14.why: 'Lås opp' is the iOS Norwegian verb for unlocking; 'one time' is already said in S10, so the button stays short beside the price.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price; 7 characters.

S16.why: What Norwegian iOS dialogs say for putting something off; it postpones without refusing.

S17.why: The label iOS uses in Norwegian for close buttons on sheets and windows.

S18.why: Verb-second order puts 'nå' first for warmth; 'ditt' agrees with the neuter 'alt'; 14 characters.

S19.s: Takk for kjøpet. Du støtter en app som én person lager.
S19.back: Thanks for the-purchase. You support an app that one person makes.
S19.why: 'Takk for kjøpet' is the fixed phrase a Norwegian shop says at the till; the second sentence names the single maker plainly.

S20.s: Velkommen tilbake. Kjøpet ditt er på plass igjen.
S20.back: Welcome back. Purchase-the your is in place again.
S20.why: 'På plass igjen' is warmer than the technical 'gjenopprettet' and greets a returning buyer the way a person would.

S21.why: Same wording as S5 so VoiceOver and the screen agree; no full stop in a spoken label.

S22.why: The noun agrees with the 5 000, always plural, and Norwegian verbs do not change with number, so it reads right for 1, 2, 5 and 21.

S23.s: Cutling er låst opp. Nå har du %@ plasser.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Now have you 5 000 places.
S23.why: App name kept as a name; 'plasser' carries through from S6 and S22.

S24.why: Passive with 'ble' blames no one; 24 characters.

S25.s: Får ikke kontakt med App Store akkurat nå. Prøv igjen om litt.
S25.back: Get not contact with App Store right now. Try again in a little.
S25.why: Subjectless 'Får ikke kontakt' is how Norwegian apps word a connection failure; 'om litt' is the spoken 'shortly'.

S26.why: Names who did not confirm, so the person is not blamed.

S27.s: Apple-kontoen på denne enheten har ingen tidligere kjøp av Cutling.
S27.back: Apple-account-the on this device-the has no earlier purchase of Cutling.
S27.why: States the fact about the signed-in account without suggesting the person did something wrong; 67 characters.

S28.s: Gratisversjonen har plass til %lld cutlinger. Lås opp Cutling én gang for å lagre så mange du vil.
S28.back: The-free-version has room for 5 cutlings. Unlock Cutling one time to save as many as you want.
S28.why: Reads well spoken by Siri; 'så mange du vil' is the idiom for as many as you like; 95 characters.

S29.why: Compact pair under the list title, same 'av' pattern as S5; 13 characters.

K1.s: Alle %lld er brukt. Lås opp i Cutling
K1.back: All 5 are used. Unlock in Cutling
K1.why: Fits the one-key capsule at 34 characters; 'Lås opp i Cutling' tells the person where the tap takes them; no closing full stop on a banner.

M1.why: Verb-led command name, as Norwegian Mac window titles and menu items are written.

M2.why: Same command as M1; the ellipsis character marks that it opens a window.

M3.why: One compound noun as a row label, the same word as on the iPhone sheet.

M4.why: The 'av' pair used everywhere else; 6 characters.

M5.why: Full status with the app name, since the free-slot label is gone once bought; 19 characters.

M6.s: Ett kjøp låser opp Cutling på iPhone, iPad og Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same device list as S8; 'ett kjøp' as in S9.

M7.s: Låst opp på iPhone, iPad og Mac med denne Apple-kontoen.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple-account-the.
M7.why: 'Apple-kontoen' as the vocabulary file spells it; participle opening suits a grey status line.

M8.s: Du kjøpte Cutling før den ble gratis, så den forblir låst opp. Takk for at du var med fra starten.
M8.back: You bought Cutling before it became free, so it remains unlocked. Thanks for that you were with from the-start.
M8.why: 'Var med fra starten' thanks an early buyer the way Norwegians say it; 'den' refers to the app; 98 characters.
